::: {.role}
Assistant Professor · Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Rochester
:::

::: {.lede}
I work on atmospheric remote sensing and connecting satellite radiances to carbon cycle processes. I lead the [Environmental Remote Sensing Lab (ERSeLab)](https://erselab.github.io) at the University of Rochester.
:::


## Explore

- [Research](research/index.qmd): greenhouse gas retrievals, validation, radiative transfer, and flux inversions.
- [Teaching](teaching.qmd): Intro to Environmental Remote Sensing.
- [Publications](publications.qmd): journal articles on satellite observations and carbon cycle inversions.
- [ERSeLab](https://erselab.github.io): the lab's projects, people and results.
- [Contact](contact.qmd)

## Background

I studied mathematics at the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma, then at the University of Oklahoma, where I earned my PhD. Along the way I found atmospheric science and the way the Earth system fits together.
